preconditions.description: The input is a list of strings.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(t, str) and len(t) == 5 and t[2] == ':' and t[:2].isdigit() and t[3:].isdigit() and 0 <= int(t[:2]) <= 23 and 0 <= int(t[3:]) <= 59 for t in alarm_times)
preconditions.description: Each element is a valid time string in HH:MM format with hours 00-23 and minutes 00-59.
The list contains at least one alarm time.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == 5 and return_value[2] == ':' and return_value[:2].isdigit() and return_value[3:].isdigit() and 0 <= int(return_value[:2]) <= 23 and 0 <= int(return_value[3:]) <= 59
postconditions.description: The output is a string in HH:MM format representing a valid time duration.

postconditions.expression: unique_minutes = sorted({int(t[:2])*60 + int(t[3:]) for t in alarm_times}); intervals = [(unique_minutes[(i+1)%len(unique_minutes)] - unique_minutes[i]) % (24*60) for i in range(len(unique_minutes))]; max_interval_minutes = max(intervals); expected_h = max_interval_minutes // 60; expected_m = max_interval_minutes % 60; return_value == f'{expected_h:02d}:{expected_m:02d}'
postconditions.description: The output represents the maximum time interval (in minutes) between consecutive alarms in a 24-hour cycle, considering the wrap-around from the last alarm to the first, formatted as HH:MM.
